stories.title: Thailand proposes $17 fee to fund tourism upgrade
stories.summary: Thailand plans to charge a 450-baht ($17) fee to foreign visitors to fund tourism infrastructure, insurance, environmental restoration and workforce development. The fee aims to shift the industry towards higher-quality and sustainable tourism, reducing reliance on limited state budgets. The proposal includes off-budget fund management with calls for transparency and industry involvement; Cabinet approval is pending after public consultation. Thailand is reviving its proposed 450-baht ($17) fee on foreign visitors as a long-term source of funding for insurance, destination renewal and a shift towards higher-quality tourism, with officials warning that continued dependence on increasingly limited state budgets could leave the industry at risk of stagnation. Revenue would be channelled into the Tourism Promotion Fund to support tourist attractions and infrastructure, environmental restoration, research, workforce development, tourism promotion and assistance for local communities. The fund would also finance insurance and health protection for foreign visitors. The Association of Thai Travel Agents (ATTA) has estimated that the fee could generate about 10 billion baht in off-budget revenue for the tourism industry. Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said the prevailing view was that Thailand needed a dedicated fund to finance improvements across the sector. “The figures clearly show that, without such a fund, Thailand’s tourism industry is approaching saturation or could begin to decline,” he said. “Relying on a state budget that becomes more limited each year would create greater constraints on competitiveness. The government therefore intends to secure off-budget funding to drive and upgrade tourism in every area.” The government wants to move Thailand’s tourism industry towards a higher-value and more sustainable model, rather than relying primarily on continued growth in visitor numbers.
